flashcards.back: It preserves the order in which one sender broadcasts messages; it does not order concurrent messages from different senders.

flashcards.front: Why can receiving differ from delivering?
flashcards.back: A protocol may buffer a received message until the selected FIFO, causal, or total-order condition is safe.
Every process delivers all broadcasts in one identical global sequence; causal order alone does not constrain concurrent messages globally.

homework.prompt: Two senders broadcast concurrent messages. Choose FIFO, causal, or total order for an application that requires every replica to show one identical history.
homework.rubric: Choose total order, explain why FIFO is sender-local, and explain why causal order leaves concurrent messages unconstrained.

homework.prompt: Explain why a broadcast implementation may receive a message but delay its delivery.
homework.rubric: Distinguish network arrival from application delivery and identify the missing ordering evidence that buffering waits for.
